name: Regalia Portrait, Title Quadrant
description: One figure holds one side of the frame at three-quarter length while the title fills the opposite upper quadrant — the subject's name over a single tagline line — and a layered distance sprawls away behind both. The figure side alternates left and right across a channel so a row of episodes does not read as one repeated image. No wordmark, no badges, no borders.
composition_guidance: Divide the 16:9 canvas along its vertical centre into a figure side and a title side, and pick the figure side deliberately per episode: alternate it left and right down a channel so that a row of episode cards never reads as one repeated image. On the figure side, one figure only, in a clearly drawn silhouette, held at three-quarter length so the cut falls at the waist or the hip, standing with the weight settled and turned slightly inward toward the centre of the frame, hands at rest or holding one simple object, the eyes level and unhurried rather than confronting the camera. The figure is backlit by low warm light so a hot bronze rim runs down the near shoulder and arm; the shadow side keeps warm bounce and never goes black. Behind and around the figure, a layered expanse fills the remaining frame in receding bands, with volumetric haze thickening band by band and broad soft rays crossing the width of the frame. The title occupies the upper quadrant on the side opposite the figure, and only that quadrant: the subject's name on the first line in bevelled metallic gold serif capitals, and directly beneath it, between two thin gold rules that run the full width of the name, one tagline line in much smaller widely spaced small capitals. Keep that quadrant's ground quiet — open atmosphere and the smallest distant form only — so nothing crosses behind the letters, and hold a clear margin between the outermost letter and both the top edge and the outer side edge. Nothing crosses the vertical centre line except the vista and the light. The frame carries exactly one figure, one name, and one tagline, and nothing else: no wordmark, no channel name, no logo, no badge, no ribbon, no numeral bug, no border, no arrow, and no third line of copy. The active Visual Style remains the final authority for medium, palette, texture, detail level and lighting; this recipe controls only the side split, the figure's crop and stance, the placement of the vista bands, and the title quadrant's position and two-line shape.
composition_rules: One figure only, in a clearly drawn silhouette, cut at three-quarter length at the waist or hip, standing on one side of the frame and turned slightly inward.
The figure side alternates left and right from episode to episode across a channel; the title always takes the upper quadrant on the opposite side.
The title is exactly two lines rendered in the image: the subject's name above, and one tagline line beneath it between two thin rules.
The layered expanse fills the rest of the frame in receding bands, hazed band by band.
A low warm light sits behind the scene, throwing broad soft rays across the frame and a hot bronze rim down the figure's near shoulder and arm.
The title quadrant stays quiet — open atmosphere and the smallest distant form — with nothing crossing behind the letters and a clear margin to the top and outer edges.
Vary the subject, the forms and the background between episodes; keep the split, the crop, the stance, the backlight and the two-line title fixed.
required_elements: One figure at three-quarter length on one side of the frame, turned slightly inward
A title of exactly two lines in the opposite upper quadrant: the subject's name over one tagline line between thin rules
A layered expanse in receding hazed bands filling the remainder of the frame
A low warm backlight behind the scene, with broad soft rays and a bronze rim on the figure's near side
avoid_elements: A wordmark, channel name, logo, badge, ribbon, numeral bug, or border of any kind
More than one figure in the foreground, or any face close to camera
A third line of copy, a date line, a number, a question mark, or an exclamation mark
Architecture, vertical forms, or rays crossing behind the letters of the title quadrant
Arrows, emoji, circles, price tags, red rings, or reaction marks
A muted grey palette, cold overcast light, flat colour, or an unfinished background
Post-render typography compositing, watermarks, or copied trade dress
Recognisable individuals, living people, or invented insignia presented as real
headline_guidance: Write the title as two lines and render both directly in the image. The first line is the subject alone — the subject the episode tells whole — in as few words as the name honestly takes, and set larger than anything else in the frame. The second line is one tagline of at most six words, naming the span, the shape, or the claim of the whole arc: the years it covers, the thing the empire was, the thing the person did. Never a question, never a number that reads as a countdown, never an exclamation, and never a tease; a listener settling toward sleep should read it as the spine of a documentary. Set the name in bevelled gold capitals and the tagline in small spaced capitals between two thin rules, and fail closed on misspelling, clipping, or any text beyond the two lines.
default_text_style: the name in bevelled metallic gold with a warm highlight along each bevel and a subtle cool chrome edge beneath, the tagline in pale bronze between two thin gold rules, both matte-metallic with no outline, no glow and no drop shadow
default_font_style: bevelled metallic gold serif capitals with faceted stems, a warm highlight running along the top of each bevel and a subtle cool chrome edge tracing the lower contour, set on one line with even tracking, and beneath them a much smaller tagline in widely spaced small capitals of the same serif, held between two thin gold rules that run the full width of the title, the tagline in pale bronze rather than gold, everything matte-metallic with no outline, no glow and no drop shadow
visual_style_guidance: This recipe is built for the hyper-detailed painterly poster look — a warm backlight, volumetric haze in every distance band, everything sharp from a near edge to the far distance, and a palette locked to gold, amber, bronze and deep crimson with cool shadow — and the quiet sky it needs behind the title quadrant comes from that style rather than from this recipe. The recipe governs only the side split and its alternation, the three-quarter-length crop and inward stance, the arrangement of the vista into receding bands, and the position and two-line shape of the title; every rendering choice of medium, palette, detail level, texture and lighting stays with the active Visual Style. A style that softens backgrounds, flattens colour, or drops to a grey palette will break this recipe, because the title quadrant then has no warm quiet ground to sit on and the distance stops reading as a whole world.
